If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then

${\int }_{-5}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-5,-1)$ and the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [-1,3].$ Using the additive property of integrals, we write

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-1).$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)\cdot 4 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,3].$ The corresponding region is a semicircle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot (2)^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =8+2\pi  \\  & =8+2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
